about: Shorts waiting to be posted, oldest first. To add one: put the .mp4 in site/media/shorts/ and add an entry here. The publisher posts the first entry not yet in posted.json. Optional "comment": posted as the first comment on each platform.

items.title: Your car payment could cost you $78,000
items.caption:
$1,000 a month for 5 years is $60,000 in car payments.
Invested instead at around 10% a year, the same money could have grown to about $78,000.
The car loses value. The investment can grow. (Returns are not guaranteed.)
items.comment: Would you still buy the car, or invest the payment instead? 👇

items.title: Start investing at 20 or 30? The gap is $298,066
items.caption:
$100 a month at 8% a year, invested until 65.
Start at 20: about $527,454. Start at 30: about $229,388.
Ten extra years of saving, just $12,000 more put in, is worth roughly $298,000.
items.comment: How old were you when you started investing? 👇

items.title: Your bank pays you 0.5% and charges you 20%
items.caption:
A traditional savings account can pay as little as 0.5% a year.
The same bank's credit card can charge 20% or more.
That gap is how banks make money from you.
items.comment: What interest does your savings account pay right now? 👇

items.title: When bread cost 200 billion marks
items.caption:
Germany, 1923. Prices doubled again and again until one loaf of bread cost about 200 billion marks.
This is what hyperinflation looks like.
items.comment: Could hyperinflation happen again today? Yes or no 👇

items.title: Your $5 coffee could be worth $226,659
items.caption:
$5 a day is $1,825 a year.
Invested instead for 30 years at 8% a year, compounded monthly, it grows to about $226,659.
Small habits, big numbers.
items.comment: Coffee or compounding: which one are you keeping? ☕👇

items.title: The worst deal in history?
items.caption:
In 1626, Manhattan was traded for goods worth about $24.
Invested at 6% a year for 400 years, that would be around $300 billion. At 8%, about $560 trillion, more than the whole world economy.
The returns are hypothetical, for illustration.
items.comment: Worst deal ever, or not? Tell us what you think 👇

items.title: $100 a month could become $228,000
items.caption:
$100 a month, invested at an assumed 10% a year for 30 years.
You put in $36,000. It could be worth about $228,000.
Start small. Start now. (Returns are not guaranteed.)
items.comment: Could you set aside $100 a month? What would you cut? 👇

items.title: The Rule of 72 in 15 seconds
items.caption:
Divide 72 by your yearly return to see how fast money doubles.
At 8%, $10,000 doubles about every 9 years: $20k, $40k, $80k, $160k by year 36.
items.comment: Did you know the Rule of 72 before this? 👇

items.title: The $5,000 debt that lasts 20 years
items.caption:
$5,000 on a card at 24% APR, paying only the minimum (interest plus 1% of the balance, $25 floor).
It takes about 19.5 years to clear, and you pay back nearly $14,000.
Pay more than the minimum, every month. Terms vary by card.
items.comment: Minimum payment or pay it off in full: what do you do? 👇

items.title: Buffett's secret nobody talks about
items.caption:
According to Morgan Housel's The Psychology of Money, $81.5 billion of Warren Buffett's $84.5 billion fortune came after his 65th birthday.
He wasn't just a great investor. He was a great investor for 70 years.
items.comment: Did you know most of his wealth came after 65? 👇

items.title: What 3% inflation does to $100
items.caption:
At 3% inflation a year, $100 today buys only about $49 worth of things in 24 years.
Cash that sits still loses value.
items.comment: What feels most expensive to you this year? 👇

items.title: Save 10% and retire with $860,000
items.caption:
Save 10% of a $50,000 salary: $5,000 a year.
Invested for 35 years at an assumed 8% a year, it could grow to about $860,000.
Pay yourself first. (Returns are not guaranteed.)
items.comment: What % of your salary do you save? 👇

items.title: The dollar lost 85% since 1970
items.caption:
What cost $1 in 1970 cost about $6.67 in 2020, based on the US consumer price index.
That's about 85% of the dollar's buying power gone.
Nobody stole it. Inflation took it, a few cents at a time.
items.comment: What did something cost when you were a kid vs now? 👇

items.title: What happened to the 1970 dollar?
items.caption:
A dollar from 1970 buys only about 12 cents' worth of things today.
That's roughly 88% of its buying power gone (US CPI data).
items.comment: Is cash a good place to keep savings long-term? 👇

items.title: Your coffee could cost you nearly $1 million
items.caption:
$5 a day is about $152 a month.
Invested at an assumed 10% a year for 40 years, that's roughly $969,000.
Don't quit coffee. Just know what your habits really cost.
items.comment: Is this worth giving up your daily coffee for? ☕👇

items.title: How your money could grow 17x
items.caption:
At an assumed 10% a year, money doubles about every 7 years.
In 30 years, that's roughly 17 times what you started with.
No lottery. Just math. (Returns are not guaranteed.)
items.comment: How many years would you let your money grow? 👇

items.title: What $1,000 becomes in 50 years
items.caption:
Put $1,000 away and don't touch it.
At an assumed 10% a year for 50 years, it could grow to about $117,000.
Patience is the real superpower.
items.comment: What would you do with $1,000 today? 👇

items.title: Why your dollar will be worth 41 cents
items.caption:
At a steady 3% inflation rate, $1 buys only about 41 cents' worth of today's goods after 30 years.
Money that sits still loses value.
items.comment: How do you protect your savings from inflation? 👇

items.title: The one-second trick that tells you when your money doubles
items.caption:
Divide 72 by your yearly return.
Savings at 2%: about 36 years. Bonds at 6%: about 12 years. Stocks at an assumed 10%: about 7 years.
Same money, totally different futures.
items.comment: Try it: what rate does your money earn, and when does it double? 👇
